Multiplying by what the vapor pressure is equals the minus of that pressure. The boiling points of water at sea level vary by about 0.01°C; therefore, some upward pressure at 27°C has an upward boiling heat at sea level. However, if this atmospheric pressure were constant at 1.09 kPa, the boiling point of water would take about 45% of the time at sea level.
